entries.title: Contentment with what comes
entries.literal_meaning: In food there is no good or bad: whatever is available in a place.
entries.explanation: The verse sets aside distinctions between preferred and less preferred food: one accepts what is available. A related passage in Jagannath Das’s Odia Bhagabata places this thought in the Avadhuta’s account to King Yadu of equanimity and the python as a teacher. Read in everyday conversation, it can counsel contentment instead of constant complaint. That everyday application is an interpretation, not an account of the saying’s first use.
entries.meaning_odia: ଯେଉଁଠି ଯାହା ମିଳେ, ତାହାକୁ ସନ୍ତୋଷରେ ଗ୍ରହଣ କରିବାର କଥା ଏହି ପଦରେ ଅଛି। ଜଗନ୍ନାଥ ଦାସଙ୍କ ଭାଗବତର ଏକ ସମ୍ପର୍କିତ ପାଠରେ ଅବଧୂତ ଯଦୁ ରାଜାଙ୍କୁ ନିଜର ସମଭାବ ଓ ଅଜଗରଠାରୁ ଶିଖିଥିବା ଧର୍ମ ବିଷୟରେ କହନ୍ତି। ସେଠାରେ ଖାଦ୍ୟ ଅଳ୍ପ ବା ବହୁତ ହେଲେ ବି ସନ୍ତୋଷ ରହେ। ଦୈନନ୍ଦିନ କଥାରେ ପଦଟି ଅନାବଶ୍ୟକ ଖୁଣ ନ ଧରି, ମିଳିଥିବା ଜିନିଷକୁ ନେଇ ଚଳିବାର ପରାମର୍ଶ ହୋଇପାରେ।
entries.usage_example: On a visit, a guest welcomes a simple meal instead of complaining that a favourite dish is missing. (Original imagined occasion.)
entries.cultural_context: The related Bhagabata text is an ascetic teaching about contentment. Its chapter9verse5 reads ଯେମନ୍ତ where the selected Incubator witness reads ଯେବଣ; keep both readings distinct. Neither this comparison nor the modern compilation establishes a first coinage or a direction of borrowing.

entries.title: Learning as wealth
entries.literal_meaning: Learning is a great treasure; children, acquire it.
entries.explanation: The verse calls learning wealth and directly addresses children. Unlike a possession handed over once, learning must be acquired through effort. The comparison gives everyday study a value beyond an immediate reward; it does not promise that education alone removes every hardship.
entries.meaning_odia: ଏଠାରେ ବିଦ୍ୟାକୁ ବଡ଼ ଧନ ବୋଲି କହି ପିଲାମାନଙ୍କୁ ତାହା ଅର୍ଜନ କରିବାକୁ ଡକାଯାଇଛି। ପଢ଼ିବା, ପଚାରିବା ଓ ଶିଖିବାରେ ଲାଗୁଥିବା ପରିଶ୍ରମକୁ ଏହି ତୁଳନା ମୂଲ୍ୟ ଦିଏ। ଏହା ଶିକ୍ଷାର ମହତ୍ତ୍ୱ ବୁଝାଏ; ପଢ଼ିଲେ ଜୀବନର ସବୁ ଅସୁବିଧା ଦୂର ହେବ ବୋଲି ନିଶ୍ଚୟତା ଦିଏନାହିଁ।
entries.usage_example: A grandparent encourages a child to spend a little time learning something new each day, even when there is no examination ahead. (Original imagined occasion.)

entries.title: A home held together by affection
entries.literal_meaning: Ah, that home is like Vaikuntha, where mutual affection remains unbroken.
entries.explanation: The verse imagines an ideal home through the affection people show one another. The important word is mutual: care is not demanded from just one person. Its heavenly comparison celebrates a quality of relationships rather than the size or expense of a house.
entries.meaning_odia: ଯେଉଁ ଘରେ ପରସ୍ପର ସ୍ନେହ ରହେ, ସେହି ଘରକୁ ପଦଟି ବୈକୁଣ୍ଠ ସହ ତୁଳନା କରେ। ଘରର ଆକାର ବା ଧନସମ୍ପତ୍ତି ନୁହେଁ, ଲୋକେ ପରସ୍ପରକୁ କିପରି ଆଦର କରନ୍ତି ତାହା ଏଠାରେ ମୁଖ୍ୟ। ସ୍ନେହ ଉଭୟ ପଟୁ ଆସିବା ଦରକାର; ଜଣଙ୍କୁ ସବୁବେଳେ ସହିବାକୁ କହିବା ଏହାର ଅର୍ଥ ନୁହେଁ।
entries.usage_example: Family members share chores and make time to listen during a difficult week; someone says this mutual care is what makes the house a home. (Original imagined occasion.)
entries.cultural_context: Vaikuntha supplies the religious comparison. This is an ideal expressed in verse, not evidence about every household or a reason to remain in a harmful relationship. No original author or work is identified by the captured entry.

entries.english_summary: Mutual affection, rather than a grand building, makes the verse’s ideal home.

entries.title: No embodied life is beyond death
entries.literal_meaning: Bearing a body in the mortal world, even a god dies.
entries.explanation: The verse uses the strongest possible contrast: even divinity does not escape death after taking bodily form in the mortal world. Read as counsel, it asks the listener to recognise the limits of embodied life. Its force is reflective and religious, not a factual account of a particular death.
entries.meaning_odia: ମର୍ତ୍ୟରେ ଦେହ ଧରିଥିଲେ ଦେବତାଙ୍କର ବି ମୃତ୍ୟୁ ହୁଏ ବୋଲି ପଦଟି କହେ। ବଡ଼ତ୍ୱ ବା ଶକ୍ତି ଥିଲେ ମଧ୍ୟ ଦେହର ସୀମା ଏଡ଼ାଇହୁଏ ନାହିଁ—ଏହି ଚିନ୍ତାକୁ ଏଥିରେ ତୀବ୍ର କରାଯାଇଛି। ଏହା ଜୀବନର ଅନିତ୍ୟତା ନେଇ ଏକ ଧାର୍ମିକ ପଦ, କୌଣସି ନିର୍ଦ୍ଦିଷ୍ଟ ଘଟଣାର ବିବରଣୀ ନୁହେଁ।
entries.usage_example: While remembering an admired elder, a family reflects quietly on how no position or achievement makes a life endless. (Original imagined occasion.)
entries.cultural_context: The wording resembles a literary or devotional maxim; the saved compilation alone does not establish its original work or oral circulation. Do not present it as medical advice or use it to dismiss someone’s grief.

entries.title: Ill will turned back on its maker
entries.literal_meaning: Whoever plans harm for another, Govinda plans harm for that person.
entries.explanation: The verse warns against deliberately wishing or planning another person’s misfortune. It imagines that ill will being answered by Govinda. This is a religious moral warning, not a guarantee that every wrongdoer will suffer or that a person’s suffering proves wrongdoing.
entries.meaning_odia: ଅନ୍ୟର ମନ୍ଦ ଚାହିଁବା ବା ମନ୍ଦ ଯୋଜନା କରିବାରୁ ପଦଟି ବାରଣ କରେ। ସେପରି ଲୋକର ମନ୍ଦ ଗୋବିନ୍ଦ ପାଞ୍ଚନ୍ତି ବୋଲି କହି ଏଥିରେ ଧାର୍ମିକ ଚେତାବନୀ ଦିଆଯାଇଛି। କାହାର ଦୁଃଖ ଦେଖି ସେ ନିଶ୍ଚୟ କିଛି ଖରାପ କରିଥିଲା ବୋଲି ରାୟ ଦେବାର ଆଧାର ଏହା ନୁହେଁ।
